title: Fizlet is out
subtitle: A 4 KB kernel budget. Six games on it.
lead: Fizlet is the micro animation and game engine for the DOM, by Chris Cooley. The kernel is 3,439 bytes gzip against a 4 KB budget, and every brick has its own budget, checked in CI. Six games run on it today. It is MIT licensed, with no runtime dependencies, ever.

body.text: Fizlet makes the page play. A hero that reacts, a diagram you can poke, a tiny game that runs on the text you are reading. The page is the board.
It is a polite guest. It plays on a page it does not own, and `destroy()` gives that page back exactly as it found it. A newer edit by the host always wins.
The fiz is fizz, the pop of an effect. The -let is small, like an applet: one small app with one job.
Every brick and every game built on Fizlet keeps the same contract, and each rule has a test.

items: **One clock per page.** Every engine shares one `requestAnimationFrame`, with a fixed step (default 60 Hz) and a catch-up cap. A long frame drops time; it never spirals.
**Bounded everything.** Pools and the event ring have a fixed capacity and refuse work when full.
**Zero steady-state allocation.** 1M kernel steps of a busy system cause 0 young-generation GCs on Node 24.
**No layout reads in the step.** Read in `read`, simulate in `step`, write in `render`.
**Change-only writes.** The ledger skips writes that change nothing.
**Pause by default.** A hidden tab, a root off screen or typing in the host's own fields pauses it. Zero CPU while paused.
**Own nothing you can't give back.** Every page change goes through the ledger, and `destroy()` restores it.
**Embed-safe.** No globals, no global styles, many engines per page.
**Budgets in CI.** Over budget, the build fails.

items.label: contract rules, each with a test

blocks.heading: Take only
blocks.subhead: One package, one import per brick: you ship only what you import. Sizes are minified + gzip, measured by `npm run size`, each against its own budget.

items.title: fizlet/input · 1,283 B
items.body: Keys, pointer and a touch stick as intents. Keys typed into the host's own fields never count.

items.title: fizlet/pad · 1,995 B
items.body: Swappable touch controls: a stick, a d-pad or move keys, plus arcade action keys.

items.title: fizlet/collide · 1,293 B
items.body: A spatial hash with overlap tests and swept circle checks, so fast shots don't tunnel.

items.title: fizlet/grid · 1,533 B
items.body: The game board: typed-array terrain, A* paths with a per-call budget, line of sight and flood fill.

items.title: fizlet/fx · 2,797 B
items.body: Pooled particles, the hero blast, pop words, scorch and shake, and named particle kinds as data.

items.title: fizlet/camera · 1,385 B
items.body: The page is the camera: eased pans and zooms, one transform through the ledger.

items.title: fizlet/sprite · 1,403 B
items.body: Pixel-art characters as data, re-tinted by palette and baked once into a capped cache.

items.title: fizlet/sound · 1,000 B
items.body: Engine events become synth cues, at most 8 voices, unlocked on a gesture.

items.title: fizlet/embed · 2,016 B
items.body: The drop-in: a hex-only palette, easter-egg triggers, lazy load, a toggle and Escape to close.

items.title: fizlet/slot · 1,856 B
items.body: Mounts a scene into a page slot: lazy start near the viewport, and reduced motion keeps the still frame.

items.title: fizlet/presence · 1,792 B
items.body: Lockstep multiplayer: only inputs cross the wire, 12 bytes each, with a state-hash desync check.

items.title: fizlet/hud · 1,320 B
items.body: Change-only readouts, meters, a feed and banners, restored on destroy.

items.title: fizlet/match · 2,599 B
items.body: Intro, count, play, pause and end on the kit's overlays, with surrender and rematch.

items.title: fizlet/rules · 1,318 B
items.body: Waves, drops, score, combo and levels. DOM-free, zero allocation.

items.title: fizlet/steer · 950 B
items.body: Movers on typed arrays: seek, flee, arrive, wander and patrol, with wall slide.

items.title: fizlet/timeline · 2,050 B
items.body: DOM choreography on the kernel clock: keyframes, stagger, labels, seek and reverse.

body.text: Also in the box: `fizlet/coach` (1,192 B) for tutorial steps and tips, and `fizlet/board-page` (4,097 B) for the host page as the board. `fizlet/arcade` (21,970 B) is the shell a page arcade game repeats, every brick it composes included. The Board UI kit is `fizlet/ui` (2,884 B plus 4,884 B of CSS), and `perf` and `debug` help in development. [See every brick](/bricks/).
Six games run on Fizlet's kernel today. Each size below is the shipped game in gzip bytes, before and after its move, from the size ledger.

items: **Battlefield Blitz:** 31,011 → 35,964 B (+16.0%). The first game built on Fizlet.

body.text: Yes, every one got bigger: 178,754 → 214,073 B together, +19.8%. The bytes buy a shared button kit, steps that never allocate, runs that replay from a seed and one shell for three games. [Each byte, and what it bought](/notes/moving-the-games-onto-a-4-kb-kernel/).
These are plans, not shipped work. Each one gets its own note, with its numbers, once it is measured.

items: **npm.** `npm install fizlet` is coming; until the first npm release, use the hosted builds or build from source.
**Multiplayer.** The `presence` brick and a room server prototype are in; a two-player Battlefield Blitz is next.
**The DOM VIRUS arcade.** The hub's home hero and the Battlefield landing arena move onto Fizlet.
**DOM Kaiju.** The first big game written on the engine from day one.

items.a: A micro animation and game engine for the DOM, by Chris Cooley. One shared loop, bounded work, zero steady-state allocation, and the page always comes back exactly as it was. MIT licensed.
The kernel is 3,439 bytes gzip, with a 4 KB budget enforced in CI. Each brick has its own budget, and a page build (kernel + slot + input + fx) measures 7,127 bytes against 7,168.
Not yet: the npm release is coming. Until then, use the hosted builds on this site or build from source with `npm ci && npm run build`.
